quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Is hearing protection needed?

options.text: No, not if you wear a helmet.
Yes, in addition to a helmet.
No, not if you carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, in addition to a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Hearing protection lets you stay safe while still hearing important sounds like car horns and sirens.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, at what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is a person age 21 or older considered legally intoxicated?
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Riding a motorcycle while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Because motorcycles are small, they may appear to be:

options.text: Going faster than they actually are.
Going slower than they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Going faster than they actually are.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's small size makes it look like it is traveling faster than it really is.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, why should you not move to the far edge of your lane?

options.text: It discourages the passing driver from cutting back too early.
It encourages the passing driver to cut back too early.
It encourages the passing driver to finish the pass quickly.
It encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It encourages the passing driver to cut back too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far edge of your lane is dangerous because it may cause the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle:

options.text: Should be done on slippery roads to avoid hazards.

questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that needs a lot of grip to do safely. Avoid sudden moves like swerving on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When riding in fog, what headlight should you use?

options.text: Switch between high and low beams

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are near.

questions.question: When going through a curve, what should you remember about lane position?

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane.
Always stay on the left side of the lane.
Always stay on the right side of the lane.
The best path may not follow the road's curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: The best path may not follow the road's curve.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change. Be ready to adjust your position in the lane at any time. The best path through a curve may not match the road's curve exactly.

questions.question: An effective face shield should NOT be:
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be clear of scratches, protect against damage, have clear views to both sides, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. An airtight shield can cause fogging that blocks your vision.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: It depends on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Choose a position based on your riding conditions. You want to keep safe space around you and be visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What is true about the center of a lane?

options.text: It is always the best place for a motorcycle.
It has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
It has oil and grease, and is never safe for riding.
It is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of each lane. On dry roads, this area usually has enough grip for motorcycles to ride safely. Avoid areas with heavy buildups of oil and grease, like busy intersections or toll booths.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the rear brake firmly while gradually increasing pressure on the front brake.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Under normal riding conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least four seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: For an eye or face shield to work well, it must:

options.text: Not allow eyeglasses to fit underneath.

questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist penetration, allow clear side views, fasten securely, allow air to pass through to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert riders to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A helmeted rider is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets, regardless of speed.

questions.question: Where should a load be placed on a motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them or place them in saddlebags. Placing loads high or against the sissy bar can raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and affect balance. Always distribute loads equally on both sides.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the tail end of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This keeps them from falling behind and allows experienced riders to watch them from behind.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are usually rectangular, white with black lettering or symbols. Riders must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: In general, how many seconds should you stay behind another vehicle?
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least three seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, why should you ride on the left side of your lane?

options.text: The right side could be slippery.
It gives you the best view of hazards in the next lane.
People don't usually expect to be passed on their left.
It places you in the rearview mirror of the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you the best view of hazards in the next lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the left portion of your lane increases your line of sight and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic when passing.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. Is this area safe for motorcyclists?

options.text: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny outside.
Always safe, no matter the weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the center of traffic lanes. This area is usually safe for motorcyclists unless the road is wet. The strip is only about two feet wide, so you can ride to one side and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: If you need to brake while turning in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Brake more gradually than you would on a straightaway.
Brake as hard as you would on a straightaway.
Wait until you are not in the curve to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gradually than you would on a straightaway.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle is leaning in a curve, the tires have less grip than when upright. Try to straighten your motorcycle before braking. If you must brake while turning, apply the brakes slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, how should you approach them?

options.text: By proceeding straight within your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: By proceeding straight within your lane.
questions.explanation: Go straight ahead in your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Turning to hit the tracks at a right angle is dangerous because it can push you into another lane.

questions.question: What happens when you brake while leaning into a curve?

options.text: It will be the same as braking on a straightaway.
You will have more traction as you lean into the curve.
You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. When the motorcycle is leaning, some tire grip is used to make the turn. This means less grip is available for stopping.

questions.question: If your front tire locks up while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you come to a full stop.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the brake lever and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake lever so the tire can grip again. Then reapply the brake.
